standard.title: Benchmarking of Environmental Monitoring Services — Guidelines (पर्यावरण निगरानी सेवाओं की बेंचमार्किंग — दिशानिर्देश)
standard.description: This standard specifies guidelines and a methodology for developing and applying a benchmarking system to evaluate environmental monitoring service providers. It applies to activities performed by environmental monitoring service providers at permanent facilities, at sites away from permanent facilities, in associated temporary or mobile facilities, or at a customer’s facility in totality. It explicitly excludes standalone testing, individual tests, or specific sampling activities from its benchmarking scope.

certification.description: Voluntary Procedural and Competence-Benchmarking Standard. Since IS 19756:2026 is an operational and management guideline standard rather than a physical consumer material, it does not carry a direct BIS 'ISI Mark' product certification stamp. However, compliance with its benchmarking index (BI) evaluation framework is highly recommended for national and state environmental authorities (like SPCBs and the CPCB), municipal corporations, and large infrastructure developers when selecting, auditing, and auditing the overall service quality and competence of private or public environmental consulting firms and laboratory partners. Precious metal hallmarking is completely inapplicable.
requirements: Applicable to all activities performed by environmental monitoring service providers at permanent facilities, at remote field sites, in associated temporary or mobile facilities, or at a customer’s facility in totality. It explicitly excludes standalone testing or individual sampling activities.

Each key criteria indicator's 'explanatory factor' must be clearly defined with a concise interpretation, be assessed from variables that are easily and reliably measured at a reasonable cost, relate to a specific geographical area and time period, and be verifiable, simple, and objective.

Scoring of each indicator must involve three or more experts/assessors making decisions on a consensus basis. The score is based on compliance to the explanatory factor and established reference benchmarks, utilizing a typical scale of: 2 - Compliance to large extent, 1 - Compliance to some extent, and 0 - No compliance.
The consensus-based indicator scores are converted into an overall Benchmarking Index (BI) for the environmental monitoring laboratory or service provider.

Reliability indicators include: Establishment (years in operation), Ownership (legal identity), Assets (ownership of land/building vs rent), Scale of operations (local, regional, or national coverage), and Project coverage (involvement in environmental audits and EIAs).

Quality indicators include: Accreditation status (covering the entire testing range under IS/ISO/IEC 17025 and holding IS/ISO 14001 certifications), Participation in accredited proficiency testing (PT) schemes per IS/ISO/IEC 17043, Internal quality controls, Talent retention, Non-conforming work handling, LIMS data management, and Management reviews.

Sustainability indicators assess: a) Environmental certifications, b) Greening the supply chain initiatives, c) Equipment suitability sustainability factors, d) Waste handling and treatment capabilities (liquid, solid, and gaseous emissions), e) Energy consumption trends and non-conventional power backups, f) Water reuse trends, and g) Assets maintenance.
